title: The Human Statue Who Keeps Turning
premise: A busker freezes every time someone says the town's name, even when nobody is watching.
pressure: The statue on Arcata Plaza cannot move whenever somebody says the town's name. His shadow can, and has just started collecting tips. 'I need a sandwich,' the busker tells you through clenched teeth. A tourist shouts ARCATA again to get a better video. The shadow holds up two fingers, either a peace sign or an invoice.
investigate: Step into the chalk circle and ask who drew its boundary
success: Under the chalk circle you uncover a municipal map marked for next Thursday, with a bus stop absent from today's streets. The shadow circles it with the toe of your shoe. 'That does not make him public property,' the busker says, accepting your photograph of the map but refusing another portrait.
failure: Your foot smears the circle and the chalk clings to your boots. The shadow follows you three embarrassing steps while the busker finally escapes. A tourist has a blurry picture, which they want to sell. You cannot prove what moved; you can refuse to be their publicity agent.
help: Get him offstage and stop the crowd filming without permission
helpOutcome: You stand between the camera phones and a man who wants to be left alone. Somebody calls that censorship. The busker calls it lunch and finally eats. Behind you, the shadow finishes its last bow to an audience of exactly one stray dog.

title: The Oyster That Won the Election
premise: A ballot kiosk announces an unopposed mollusk; only the losing candidate can hear its platform.
pressure: An oyster has won a town election despite having no address, pulse or apparent interest in public office. The defeated candidate insists the voting machine is broken; the fishers would prefer to read the platform first.
investigate: Ask for a translation and compare it with the actual ballot language
success: The manifesto turns out to be a tide forecast written in the language of municipal ordinances. Next week's low water is on it. Next week's low water has not been scheduled.
failure: The translator admits they guessed at half the clauses. The oyster closes its shell and the defeated candidate reluctantly agrees the vote needs an audit.
help: Hold an open meeting where the affected shoreline users speak first
helpOutcome: A wheelchair user, two fishers and the harbormaster agree on real access hours. The oyster abstains, quite possibly for tax reasons.

title: The Man Selling Used Fog
premise: A persuasive stranger can bottle exactly one memory in a mason jar.
pressure: A fog seller has priced a jar of LAST BUS at twelve dollars, plus whatever the buyer has forgotten. A woman recognizes the handwriting on its label but says the memory is hers to give, not his to sell. You recognize the street inside. Neither of you recognizes the night.
investigate: Ask the woman whether she wants the jar opened, then check the route number
success: She chooses to open it. The memory shows a future bus terminal drawn on a folded transfer; you copy the route, not her private recollection.
failure: The seal snaps and the picture dissolves. You save the damp label, and the woman remembers which driver once used that handwriting.
help: Help the owners reclaim the jars without making their memories a public show
helpOutcome: The seller returns three jars and cancels his demonstration. The woman keeps hers closed. Reclaiming something does not oblige her to explain it.

title: Plaza Clock, Wrong County
premise: The clock strikes thirteen; everyone else insists it always has.
pressure: Arcata's plaza clock strikes thirteen. Half the shops hang CLOSED FOR THE OTHER COUNTY signs, and a delivery driver discovers that both his address and his lunch break have been reassigned. The vegetables are real. So is the ticket he will get for parking nowhere.
investigate: Compare the clock with the bus schedule and three independent shop receipts
success: Four clocks skipped the same minute. The bus route prints a detour to a street under the bay, while the driver's receipts prove this delivery happened.
failure: Your own watch briefly runs backward, then has the decency to stop. A shopkeeper signs a statement recording exactly when the street signs changed.
help: Find the driver a safe place to unload before his entire route expires
helpOutcome: A grocer opens cold storage for the stranded produce and the driver phones every customer. The county may have split in two; the lettuce does not have to suffer.

title: Audience of One Hundred and One
premise: A midnight screening has one more shadow than ticket holders.
pressure: The midnight screening has sold one hundred tickets, but an extra shadow keeps changing seats. It wears a coat that none of the patrons brought, and the usher fears management will blame her for overselling a ghost.
investigate: Compare the ticket stubs against the moving shadow's seat numbers
success: One seat is reserved on a ticket dated next Friday. The name is smudged, but the price is exactly what a ticket will cost after the announced increase.
failure: The emergency lights come on and every shadow looks entirely respectable. Two patrons independently remember the same empty coat, and the usher keeps their descriptions.
help: Give the usher permission to stop the film and ask the audience what they actually saw
helpOutcome: The screening pauses, the usher gets a second witness, and the uncounted guest settles into the last row. Nobody is asked to buy another ticket on its behalf.

title: Rocky Horror, Actual Horror
premise: A shadow-cast prop gains agency and demands better stage directions.
pressure: At the Minor Theatre fundraiser, an alien stage prop refuses the stabbing scene. The director says cancelling will cost the volunteer crew its rent money. 'What do you think the stabbing costs us?' the understudy asks, holding a prop knife with the safety catch broken. The alien is not speaking, but it has carefully underlined the injury clause in a union handbook.
investigate: Ask the prop and cast to rehearse a version everyone can consent to
success: The understudy rewrites the cue, the alien nods by tipping its painted antenna, and the scene works without a blade near anyone's throat. In exchange it hands the stage manager a warehouse address dated tomorrow. 'A useful tip is not permission to send an unpaid intern,' she says, and locks the script in her desk.
failure: The alien will not take its mark. The crowd laughs until the understudy shows them the old script, its dangerous direction signed by nobody who still works here. The director accuses you of sabotaging the fundraiser. You have not fixed opening night; you have helped the crew refuse a bad rehearsal.
help: Replace the dangerous effect and give the crew an actual say
helpOutcome: You swap the stabbing for a collapsing paper moon and let the crew vote on the change. The audience laughs harder at the cheap moon than at last year's expensive blood effect. The director is furious about artistic compromise. The understudy counts the uninjured cast and calls it a standing ovation.

title: Simplex's Encore
premise: A phantom theater cat walks through the projection beam and selects tomorrow's film.
pressure: At the Minor, a cat-shaped absence pads across the projector beam and selects a reel about a theater fire. The last frame is tomorrow's date and a harbor weather alert. The projectionist is paid to protect the film, not to decide whether a ghost understands forecasts.
investigate: Compare the final frame with the archive catalog and the current harbor advisory
success: The reel's stock is decades old, but the warning names a berth added last spring. You preserve the frame number and report the risk without claiming a prediction.
failure: The reel tangles before you can photograph the date. The projectionist saves the leader strip, where one impossible paw print remains in the emulsion.
help: Help staff safeguard the reel and circulate the practical weather warning
helpOutcome: The reel goes into a proper canister; the advisory reaches the harbor desk. The cat chooses the next feature and declines to explain its taste.

title: The Film That Watches Back
premise: A lost reel depicts the player's next choice, badly subtitled.
pressure: A lost film reel projects the decision you are about to make, complete with a subtitle calling you a coward. Then it shows a different decision and prints COWARD again. The actor playing you turns toward the booth. 'Could someone tell the writer I have a contract?' The projectionist wants to burn the reel. A teenager in the back row asks to see what happens if the actor walks offscreen.
investigate: Stop the projector and inspect the scene frame by frame before trusting a subtitle
success: Frame by frame, you find a third answer hidden in a cut where the actor refuses both scripted choices. The background shows an unbuilt Trinidad sign, which remains wrong across every rewind. 'At last,' the actor says from the screen, 'a continuity error with a conscience.' You keep the sequence, not its accusation.
failure: The film breaks at the exact moment you reach for the projector. You have the damaged strip, not proof of your future. The audience starts repeating the subtitle anyway. You ask who profits when every option is labeled cowardice; nobody answers, which tells you more about the audience than the film.
help: Ask the audience to write an ending that does not assume they know anyone's heart
helpOutcome: You let the audience propose new lines while the projectionist repairs the reel. The room argues until a child says, 'Maybe they're frightened and still choosing.' The actor sits on the projected curb to listen. No one agrees on the correct ending. For one minute, nobody tries to decide yours.

title: The Trail with Two Trailheads
premise: A jogger repeatedly emerges at the trailhead they have not reached.
pressure: A jogger comes out of the Community Forest at the wrong trailhead, then does it again without crossing the road between them. His watch claims six uphill miles. He keeps asking whether he has been running away from the same tree for an hour.
investigate: Mark the junctions and compare his watch with a second trail map
success: A trail marker ages decades between two photographs taken seconds apart. You record both timestamps, then turn back while there is still daylight.
failure: The loop deposits you at your starting point. Your map is unchanged but there are fresh footprints beside yours, in a size neither of you wears.
help: Help the jogger reach a staffed exit instead of testing the loop again
helpOutcome: A volunteer meets you at the gate, checks the jogger is warm and accounted for, and posts a temporary notice. The forest keeps its extra trail to itself.

title: The Deer in the Reflective Vest
premise: A park volunteer gives safety instructions for events scheduled in 1897.
pressure: A deer in a reflective vest stops hikers beside a slope and hands over a bridge-closure notice dated 1897. One corner bears today's trail maintenance number. A family with a stroller is approaching the washed-out bank.
investigate: Compare the old notice with the current trail map and inspect the bank from safe ground
success: The present-day drainage line crosses the vanished bridge footing. You photograph fresh cracks and give the maintenance crew an exact location.
failure: A gust takes the notice before you can photograph its seal. You still mark a crack widening under the trail edge and tell the crew what you saw.
help: Turn walkers back and help volunteers mark a safe detour
helpOutcome: The stroller and everyone behind it take the longer route. The deer checks the barriers twice, which is more than the county budget allows.

title: Mushroom Neighborhood Watch
premise: A fungus network files very specific complaints about the living.
pressure: A row of mushrooms has filed a noise complaint against a drainage pipe below the Community Forest trail. Each cap holds a tiny slip of paper. The sound is not loud, but the slope downhill is newly wet and a volunteer has found sediment in the creek.
investigate: Trace the pipe's outflow with the volunteer without digging into the fungal bed
success: The pipe bypasses an old settling ditch. A future-dated work order supplies a useful number, not permission to disturb the site.
failure: Rain turns your dye test into a green wash that cannot prove where the pipe starts. The mushrooms file a second complaint, this one naming your methods. A volunteer photographs the seep with a ruler and asks you to sign the failed test log. You do.
help: Help the trail crew reroute foot traffic while they inspect the discharge
helpOutcome: A short closure keeps boots off the colony and lets the crew sample the water. The mushrooms amend their complaint to include an appreciation for signage.

title: Campfire Without a Camp
premise: Invisible campers gossip about the player's future over cold ash.
pressure: Six camp chairs ring ash cold enough to hold rainwater. Invisible campers are debating a future betrayal with startling confidence; you hear the name of a person you have yet to meet. A real hiker sits down, hoping the voices know where her missing friend went.
investigate: Write down the disputed names and ask the voices for a verifiable trail detail
success: Their arguments disagree about everything except a ranger-station marker. The hiker recognizes it and calls the station with a precise search area.
failure: Every voice talks at once and the names become useless. Beneath one chair you find a fresh boot print headed toward the marked path.
help: Stay with the hiker and contact the ranger rather than audition for the prophecy
helpOutcome: The ranger gets a description and a last known location; the hiker has company while she waits. The empty chairs argue about whether this counts as betrayal.

title: Office Hours with a Visiting Moon
premise: A lecturer's guest speaker insists it is the actual moon on sabbatical.
pressure: The visiting lecturer is a moon no larger than a grapefruit, sitting at the campus podium beneath a borrowed desk lamp. It has scheduled office hours during a partial eclipse. An astronomy student worries the class will believe the guest's charming false claims about the tides.
investigate: Ask the moon to distinguish its anecdotes from the measurements in the syllabus
success: It admits one celebrated eclipse story is borrowed. The student corrects the data sheet while the moon supplies a startlingly accurate new observation.
failure: The moon refuses a citation and rolls beneath the lectern. The class keeps the conflicting readings for later comparison instead of voting on astronomy.
help: Help the professor hold a discussion where students can ask questions safely
helpOutcome: The student leads a demonstration with a lamp and two oranges. The moon volunteers to be the third orange and accepts peer review badly.

title: Dorm Room 404
premise: A missing dorm room has a remarkably active meal plan.
pressure: The housing office insists Dorm 404 does not exist. Someone leaves shoes against the blank wall, a meal card is charged three times a day, and a resident adviser has been told to stop asking after the missing student. The shoes are still wet from the rain.
investigate: Check the meal-plan charges with housing staff before guessing who lives there
success: The account belongs to a student enrolled next autumn, with an emergency-contact number that rings inside the wall. The registrar logs the anomaly rather than inventing a disciplinary case.
failure: The card is deactivated and dinner appears at the wall anyway. A cafeteria worker signs the receipt and asks the housing office to check that somebody is eating.
help: Arrange a welfare check that gives the unseen resident privacy and a safe way to answer
helpOutcome: The resident adviser leaves food, a written question and the number for a real person. By morning the reply says THANK YOU FOR KNOCKING. Nobody tries to tear down the wall.

title: The Thesis Defense of the Dead
premise: An academic committee includes someone who never graduated and never died.
pressure: The thesis committee's fourth examiner appears on no enrollment ledger, obituary or faculty roster. She has nevertheless written thirty-seven devastating margin notes, and the candidate is minutes from a defense whose result determines their funding.
investigate: Check the cited sources in the mysterious examiner's critique
success: Most are solid; one quotes an article not yet published. The candidate gets time to verify it rather than having a dissertation rewritten by a ghost.
failure: One citation sends you through a circular archive index. You flag it as unverifiable; the candidate can answer the substantive question without pretending otherwise.
help: Ask the chair to make the defense fair despite the extra examiner
helpOutcome: The chair rules the phantom's notes advisory and extends the candidate's time. The examiner nods, disappointed to discover due process.

title: The Mascot Disputes Biology
premise: The campus mascot begins providing accurate but unwanted zoological advice.
pressure: Between cheers, the campus mascot delivers a lecture on an animal no one on the field can identify. Its drawings are persuasive. Its microphone is feeding the speech over the emergency instructions, while the student inside the costume looks desperate for water.
investigate: Ask for the field notebook and compare the sketches with the campus collections
success: A sketch records markings from a specimen accessioned tomorrow. The curator takes the copy; nobody calls it proof of a living animal.
failure: The mascot forgets the species name as soon as its head comes off. The student retains a drawing with one unusually exact habitat note.
help: Get the student out of the overheated suit and return the microphone to safety announcements
helpOutcome: The medic checks the student; the game resumes with a replacement announcer. The mascot's written complaint about inaccurate birds remains on the bulletin board.

title: Finals Week from Another Timeline
premise: Exams arrive before classes and the university refuses refunds.
pressure: Final exams appear in students' inboxes before their first lecture. Every question concerns a civic decision nobody has publicly proposed. A teaching assistant is fielding panicked emails from students who think this is a trick to deny them financial aid.
investigate: Compare the exam metadata with course records and a public council agenda
success: One question cites a meeting room that will not open until next month. The registrar can investigate the timestamp without grading anyone's future.
failure: The files redate themselves when downloaded. A student has saved a paper printout bearing the original header, enough to start a fair review.
help: Help students get the exams paused without exposing private grades
helpOutcome: The instructor postpones the test and offers an actual syllabus. A student frames the premature F as a warning against group projects.
